To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the normalized density and temperature profiles can be parametrized with log additive models.
the temperature profile is peaked by ICRH, and the density profile is broadened by high heating powers, especially ICRF.
the density and temperature profiles of the JointEuropean Torus (Jet) are parametrised using log additive models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the parametrization of the temperature and density profile shapes in the JET tokamak plasma.
the development of an empirical model for predicting the temperature and density profiles in the JET tokamak from a limited set of control variables.
the parametrization and prediction of the JET electron temperature and density profile shapes using the control variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the density and temperature profiles of JET plasmas are well described by log linear additive models in the parameters n/q95 and Bt for density, and heating type, Zeff, Bt and power per particle for the temperature profile.
the temperature profiles are strongly dependent on the heating method, and the density profiles depend primarily on the current, Ip, and the ratio n/q95.
the shape of both density and temperature profiles depends on the heating type, the current and the density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the density profile shape depends on the plasma current, the heating type, the heating power, the line average density, and the edge safety factor.
the temperature profile shapes are strongly influenced by the heating type and the density profile shapes are influenced by the edge safety factor and the current.
the density profiles in L mode are primarily determined by the ratio n/Bt, while the temperature profiles are determined primarily by the heating type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temperature and density profiles can be parametrized in terms of the control variables, and that the profiles can be used to predict the plasma behavior in JET.
the shape of the JET density and temperature profiles is determined primarily by a small number of control variables.
the density profile shapes are more sensitive to control parameters than the temperature profiles.
